notes.1: 0.3 returns ENOTCONN after reset consumed by Write. Poller commit changes this to an indefinite wait. Parent and commit independently tested 5 times with both Go versions.
notes.8: SocketConfig.NotificationHandler did not exist in 0.3. The public NewSCTPConn(fd, handler) constructor was used to test the same subscription loss.
notes.9: Missing nil-metadata handling exists in 0.3: Go1.18.10 panics with SENDER_DRY(0x8009); the same 0.3 source on Go1.26.10 returns stale metadata bytes.
notes.13: 0.3 returns a non-nil actual pointer with fd=-1 on Accept error. The typed-nil interface specifically appears at the poller commit. This remains P3 nonblocking, not a functional regression.
notes.15: ErrUnsupported is already missing on native Linux in 0.3. Listener.SyscallConn is absent on all 0.3 targets and was not a supported API then. Its cross-platform parity gap appears when 805d8b81dda51bec54acdc686b39a0c020fa799e adds the Linux method; first containing fork tag is 0.4.
notes.16: Unsupported Close leaves the supplied SCTP fd open in 0.3. The explicit ownership documentation was added later; the resource behavior already exists.

test_adaptations: Use existing public fd constructor for NotificationHandler because the 0.3 SocketConfig field is absent.
Force peer ABORT with raw SO_LINGER+close, because 0.3 Close invokes shutdown before closing. Suppress owner cleanup after raw close to avoid reused-fd cleanup.
Use Go1.18-compatible test syntax and direct socket timeouts; do not backport runtime polling into the 0.3 library.
Use non-nil local address for nil-remote test to avoid the independent old nil-laddr Control-hook panic.
